title: Fox Renews 'Animal Control' & 'Going Dutch
text:
Fox Bets Big on Laughs: What the “ Animal Control ” and “Going Dutch” Renewals Mean for the Future of Comedy In a move that signals a continued commitment to comedy, Fox has officially renewed both Animal Control and Going Dutch . But what does this decision really mean for the network’s strategy, the future of sitcoms, and your viewing schedule in the 2025-2026 season?
“Animal Control” Season 4: A Comedy flagship Sails On Animal Control , starring Joel mchale, will be returning for its fourth season.This renewal comes as no surprise to industry insiders, as the show has become a cornerstone of Fox’s live-action comedy programming. Its success extends far beyond American borders, having been sold to over 70 international territories. Think of it as the “Modern Family” of animal-themed sitcoms, but with a distinctly Fox edge.
Why “Animal Control” Works: A Deep Dive The show’s premise – a group of Animal Control workers navigating the absurdities of both animals and humans – resonates with a broad audience. Joel McHale ‘s portrayal of Frank Shaw,the cynical ex-cop with an uncanny ability to understand animals,provides a perfect blend of sarcasm and heart. It’s a formula that’s proven successful, drawing viewers in with its relatable characters and laugh-out-loud scenarios.
Did you know? Animal Control more than doubles its Live+Same Day ratings with in-season streaming on Hulu. this highlights the growing importance of streaming platforms in the success of network television. The show’s international appeal is also a significant factor in its renewal. Its presence on channels like Channel 4 in the UK, Foxtel and Binge in Australia, CBC in Canada, and TVNZ in New zealand demonstrates its universal comedic themes. It’s not just an American show; it’s a global hit.
“Going Dutch” Season 2: A Second chance for Transatlantic Humor The renewal of Going Dutch , starring Denis leary, for a second season was less of a sure thing. While the show launched strongly, retaining nearly 100% of its Animal Control lead-in audience for its premiere, it experienced a decline in linear viewership throughout its first season. However, Fox’s ownership of the show ultimately played a crucial role in its return.
The “going Dutch” Gamble: Why fox Is Sticking With It Going Dutch centers on U.S. Army Colonel Patrick quinn (Leary), who is reassigned to a quirky Army base in the Netherlands. The show’s humor stems from the clash of cultures and Quinn’s attempts to impose order on a group of eccentric military personnel. While it may not have achieved the same level of widespread success as Animal Control , its unique premise and Denis Leary’s comedic talent offer potential for growth.
Expert Tip: Shows that are wholly-owned by a network have a significant advantage when it comes to renewal decisions. The network can leverage international sales and streaming rights to recoup costs and generate revenue, making them more likely to invest in a second season. Denis Leary’s comments about the 10-episode season length also shed light on the changing landscape of television production. the shorter season allows him to pursue other projects and maintain a higher level of quality control. This trend towards shorter seasons is becoming increasingly common in the industry, as networks and creators prioritize quality over quantity.
The Bigger Picture: Fox’s Comedy Strategy for 2025-2026 The renewals of Animal Control and Going Dutch suggest that Fox may not be looking to pick up any new half-hour comedies for the 2025-2026 season. This indicates a strategic focus on building upon existing successes rather than taking risks on unproven concepts. It’s a calculated move that reflects the competitive nature of the television industry.
What This Means for Aspiring Comedy Writers For aspiring comedy writers, this news might potentially be disheartening. However, it also presents an opportunity to focus on creating high-quality scripts that stand out from the crowd. With fewer slots available, the competition will be fierce, but the rewards for success will be even greater. Think of it as the “Hunger Games” of sitcom writing – may the best script win.
The Rise of workplace Humor: A Trend in Comedy Michael Thorn, president of Fox Television Network , emphasized the importance of “irreverent, fun workplace humor” in the success of Animal Control and Going Dutch . This highlights a growing trend in comedy towards shows that explore the dynamics of the workplace. From “ The Office ” to “ Parks and Recreation ,” workplace comedies have consistently resonated with audiences.
Why Workplace Comedies Work: A Psychological Outlook Workplace comedies offer a relatable and ofen cathartic experience for viewers. They allow us to laugh at the absurdities of our own work lives and connect with characters who share similar struggles. The shared experience of navigating office politics, dealing with tough bosses, and forming friendships with colleagues provides a rich source of comedic material.
Beyond the Renewals: Other Fox Programming Updates In addition to the comedy renewals, Fox has also picked up its freshman drama doc for a rare 22-episode order and the Canadian-made rookie Murder In a Small Town . Moreover, the network has secured a mega-deal for its animated titles The Simpsons, Family Guy , and Bob’s Burgers , as well as a four-season renewal for American Dad! this demonstrates Fox’s commitment to a diverse range of programming, from animated comedies to medical dramas.
The Future of Fox: A Balanced Approach Fox’s programming strategy for the 2025-2026 season appears to be a balanced approach, combining established hits with promising new shows. By investing in both comedy and drama, the network aims to appeal to a broad audience and maintain its position as a leading player in the television industry. It’s a strategy that reflects the ever-changing landscape of entertainment, where streaming services and customary networks compete for viewers’ attention.
Reader Poll: Which Fox comedy are you most excited to see return? Animal Control Going Dutch Both! Pros and Cons of Fox’s Comedy Strategy pros: Stability: Renewing established shows provides stability and predictability for viewers. Proven success: Animal Control has a proven track record of success, both domestically and internationally. Network Ownership: Fox’s ownership of Going Dutch allows for greater control over its distribution and revenue potential. Focus on Quality: Shorter season lengths allow for greater quality control and creative freedom. Cons: Lack of Innovation: Focusing on existing shows may limit opportunities for new and innovative comedies. Risk aversion: The decision to forgo new half-hour comedies may be seen as risk-averse. Potential for Stagnation: Relying too heavily on established shows could lead to creative stagnation. “Going Dutch” Uncertainty: The show’s initial struggles raise questions about its long-term viability. FAQ: Your Burning Questions Answered Will there be any new comedy shows on Fox in 2025-2026? Based on current information, Fox may not be looking to pick up any new half-hour comedies for the 2025-2026 season, focusing instead on its renewed shows.
Why was “Animal Control” renewed for a fourth season? Animal Control has become a flagship comedy for Fox, achieving both domestic and international success. Its strong ratings and broad appeal make it a valuable asset for the network.
What is “Going Dutch” about? Going dutch centers on U.S. Army Colonel Patrick Quinn, who is reassigned to a quirky Army base in the Netherlands. The show explores the clash of cultures and Quinn’s attempts to impose order on a group of eccentric military personnel.
Why was “Going Dutch” renewed despite its initial struggles? Fox’s ownership of Going Dutch played a significant role in its renewal. The network can leverage international sales and streaming rights to recoup costs and generate revenue.
What does Denis Leary think about the shorter season length of “Going Dutch”? Denis Leary has expressed his appreciation for the 10-episode season length, as it allows him to pursue other projects and maintain a higher level of quality control.
What is workplace humor, and why is it popular? Workplace humor refers to comedies that explore the dynamics of the workplace. These shows are popular because they offer a relatable and often cathartic experience for viewers, allowing them to laugh at the absurdities of their own work lives.
What other shows has Fox renewed for the 2025-2026 season? In addition to Animal Control and Going Dutch , Fox has also picked up its freshman drama Doc for a rare 22-episode order and the Canadian-made rookie Murder In a small Town . Moreover, the network has secured a mega-deal for its animated titles The Simpsons, Family Guy , and Bob’s Burgers , as well as a four-season renewal for American Dad!
Fox’s Comedy Bet: A Q&A With TV Expert Alana Bloom on “animal Control,” “Going Dutch,” and the Future of Sitcoms Keywords: Fox, Animal Control, Going Dutch, Comedy, Sitcoms, Television, Renewals, Streaming, Workplace Humor, TV Industry
Time.news: Fox recently renewed both “Animal Control” and “Going Dutch.” What does this double renewal tell us about Fox’s comedy strategy, and what does it mean for viewers like me in the 2025-2026 season? We’ve invited Alana Bloom, a seasoned TV industry analyst, to unpack this news for us. Alana, welcome!
alana Bloom: Thanks for having me! it’s an captivating move by Fox, and it speaks volumes about their priorities.
Time.news: Let’s start with the obvious. “Animal Control” season 4 – was this renewal a given? What makes it so accomplished? Any thoughts?
Alana bloom: Absolutely. “Animal Control” has become a genuine comedy flagship for fox. Its success is multifaceted. The premise itself – quirky animal control workers – is relatable and allows for endless comedic scenarios. Joel McHale’s performance brings a cynical charm that anchors the show. Plus, its proven success in manny international markets provides a substantial revenue stream.Think about it – being sold to over 70 countries? That’s impressive. It gives Fox confidence.
Time.news: The article highlights that “Animal Control” more than doubles its live ratings with streaming on Hulu. How critically important is that streaming boost in the current TV landscape?
Alana Bloom: Critical. Live ratings are onyl part of the picture now. Streaming is where a huge chunk of the audience is, and that in-season streaming data is what networks are very carefully watching. In fact, that streaming boost is likely one of the biggest drivers in ensuring that “Animal Control” was renewed.
Time.news: “Going Dutch” Season 2 was less certain, according to our sources. Why did Fox stick with it, even with its initial linear viewing struggles? Isn’t that unusual?
Alana Bloom: Yes and no. “Going Dutch” got off to a promising start,holding its “Animal Control” lead-in audience really well. But that advantage waned off slightly as the season went on. Its renewal really demonstrates the advantage that comes with a network owning the production. Fox controls ALL associated rights with “Going Dutch” – international sales, streaming deals, everything. They can be much more flexible as an inevitable result. moreover,Denis Leary is an established name,which carries its own weight.Networks like to remain in the Denis Leary business.
Time.news: The article touches on Denis Leary’s recognition for the 10-episode season order. Is this shorter season length a trend, and what does it mean for the industry?
Alana Bloom: Absolutely a trend! Streamers are driving this evolution of television production. Shorter seasons allow creators to focus on quality,explore complex storylines,and attract A-list talent,who are,for example,less likely to commit to a traditional 22 episode season. It also gives the talent more adaptability to pursue other projects. So expect to see more and more shows adopting this format.
Time.news: So, are we to believe that Fox is unlikely to pick up any entirely new half-hour comedies for 2025-2026? That might concern budding comedy writers. What advice do you have for them if they’re trying to break into the industry?
Alana Bloom: this situation presents interesting challenges and opportunities.Networks are risk-averse because the competition is fierce. Still, comedies are perennially popular, so I suspect their will be new comedy content on Fox. The advice I would give writers is to focus on developing exceptionally well-writen, unique scripts. Understand current trends – workplace humor, for sure, because executives find them reliable – but also look for fresh angles and diverse perspectives. Don’t be afraid to be bold, but make sure it’s also commercially viable. Also, explore writing for streaming platforms or cable networks, where there might be more opportunities for new voices. Try to partner with an established name for better chances of getting your foot in the door!
Time.news: The article mentions Michael Thorn’s emphasis on “irreverent,fun workplace humor.” Why is that genre so consistently successful?
Alana Bloom: Workplace comedies offer worldwide appeal and the catharsis of office politics. Most adults have employment experiences that inform their perspectives. Workplace comedies help viewers laugh at shared experiences, make them feel understood, and offer relatable characters,
Time.news: What are the biggest pros and cons of Fox’s apparent comedy strategy for the upcoming season?
Alana Bloom: The pros are stability and the reliability of proven successes. Fox knows what they’re getting with “Animal Control,” and owning “Going Dutch” gives them financial flexibility. Shorter seasons can lead to higher quality, too. The cons? A potential lack of innovation and risk aversion. Relying too heavily on established shows can lead to creative stagnation, and “Going Dutch’s” initial struggles do raise some questions about its longer-term viability.
Time.news: Final thoughts? What’s the one thing readers should take away from this discussion?
Alana Bloom: The television landscape is constantly evolving,and networks are adapting. Fox’s strategy reflects this change, prioritizing familiar faces while exploring new avenues for revenue and viewership, notably in the streaming realm. This isn’t necessarily a bad thing, but it means aspiring creators need to be more strategic and innovative than ever to break through.
